analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (flowchart nodes, a paragraph on the proactive sweep, retained KV segments counted as reclaimable) and docs/architecture/inference.md (new paragraph at head lines 808-823 on parked 64 MiB paged-KV segments and zero-fill-on-demand host pages). No code, key handling, attestation, authorization or wire contract changes, so no regression in the threat model's controls can be shown from the supplied evidence.

The documented behavior could touch T-028 (residual KV data in memory) and A-001. Free KV segments are parked per pool, up to min(2 GiB, grant/8), outside the grant, floor and ledger charge, and reinstalled for the next admission of the same size class. The docs do not say whether parked segments are zeroed or overwritten before reuse. New segments wrap zero-fill-on-demand host pages. Because the parked backing is process-local, and T-028 already accepts residual data in GPU memory for the same process owner, this is not a new boundary crossing on the evidence supplied. Reuse across different consumers' requests within the process is already the baseline in T-028.

The parked-memory accounting is outside the ledger charge. It is documented as counted reclaimable at load admission (CBv2RetainedKVSegments.retainedBytes) and dropped on pressure, a refused charge, a cold load or 30 s idleness. A possible availability gap is that uncharged parked memory could crowd out other work. The doc says release is wired into pressure and load paths, but I cannot verify the Swift implementation (EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift, PagedKVGroup.swift, KVPoolReclaimer), which is not supplied. The DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION=0 and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP=0 kill switches are operator env vars with no new trust boundary.

The TTFT changes might subtly alter timing behavior relevant to T-041's accepted oracle. They are not a prefix-cache or at-rest change, and the SSD tier, TTL, HMAC names and scope are untouched. The next pass should review the underlying code for zeroing semantics of reinstalled segments and the bounds on parked memory.
